clue.text: Stick with French red somewhere in Louisiana

parts.note: a baton is a short stick, as carried by a conductor or relay runner
rouge is the French word for red

explanation.surface: A cook is told to combine a stick with French red wine somewhere down in Louisiana.
explanation.definitionFit: The state capital of Louisiana is a city, so it is fairly described as a place there.

clue.text: Up in old part of Yorkshire

definitions.meaning: up can mean on horseback, as a jockey who is up is in the saddle and mounted
Yorkshire was historically divided into three administrative districts, North, East and West

explanation.surface: Someone is up in an old part of Yorkshire, perhaps out on the moors.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire is an English county; its three historic divisions were each called by this name, from an Old Norse word for a third.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: being mounted on a horse, and one of the three historic divisions of the county.

clue.text: I take off from island with German ace, going over to Rome initially

indicators.note: in a down clue the ace goes over, that is sits above, the pieces that follow it

parts.note: mit is the German word for with
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the word Rome is used

explanation.surface: A pilot leaves an island with a German flying ace, heading over to Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I take off' reads like a pilot departing, but it is what a mimic says: to take off is to impersonate.
explanation.definitionFit: A mimic might say this of themselves, since taking someone off means copying their mannerisms for fun.

clue.text: Take out permit to enter Scottish river

indicators.note: to enter tells us the word for permit goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee flows through Aberdeenshire to the sea at Aberdeen
to let is to permit or allow

explanation.surface: An angler takes out a permit to fish a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove text or data is to strike it out or erase it, the same as taking it out.

clue.text: Meal in Spanish city entertaining group of people, not British

indicators.note: entertaining means holding, as a host holds guests, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: León is a city in north-west Spain

indicators.note: not British says to drop B, the abbreviation for British

parts.note: a bunch can be a group of people, as in a friendly bunch

explanation.surface: A meal in a Spanish city where the hosts entertain a group, with no British guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' looks like hospitality but means holding inside; 'not British' drops the B to leave UNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for the midday meal, so it is a kind of meal.

clue.text: Woman protected by assumed name

indicators.note: protected by means held inside, so the letters lie within the words assumed name

explanation.surface: A woman is shielded by living under an assumed name.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so a crossword stands it for any woman.

clue.text: Mud, it's spread across a sports ground

indicators.note: across means the scrambled letters stretch over, so around, the letter a
spread means the letters of the words mud and it's are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: After rain, mud is smeared all over a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges MUDITS, and 'across' puts that round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A large arena with tiered seating built for sporting events.

clue.text: Extremely amusing team parting company

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
splitting means separating, as when a couple go their own ways

explanation.surface: A team breaking up, which observers find hilarious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so funny it makes one laugh hard enough to ache, so hilarious.

clue.text: New cure must contain trouble in country

indicators.note: must contain means the rearranged letters hold the word for trouble inside them
new means the letters of the word cure are put into a fresh order

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble, as in much ado

explanation.surface: A new cure is bound to cause trouble somewhere in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the four letters to ECUR, which 'must contain' the word for trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic on the Pacific coast of South America, so it is a nation.

clue.text: Bishop, yes, and king, always on edge

parts.note: right is used as agreement, like yes
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex
ever means always, as in ever hopeful
the end of something is its edge or limit

explanation.surface: A bishop and a king, both always on edge, perhaps in a game of chess.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the formal title and style used before the name of an Anglican diocesan prelate.

clue.text: Following party, ring petite Cockney flower girl

indicators.note: following tells us the rest comes after the word for party

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
the letter O is round like a ring
petite means small or little

explanation.surface: After a party, someone phones a petite Cockney girl who sells flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza, the Cockney flower seller in Shaw's Pygmalion and My Fair Lady; Cockney is the working-class accent of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Eliza, the flower girl from Shaw's play who is taught to speak like a lady.

clue.text: Clash with large family, foremost in Glasgow

parts.note: a clan is an extended family group, especially in Scotland

indicators.note: foremost in means only the first letter of the word Glasgow is taken

explanation.surface: A feud with a big Scottish family, the leading one in Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud metallic ringing noise, as when cymbals or swords strike together.

clue.text: Indicate lack of interest in Welsh rugby

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words Welsh rugby, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: Someone signals they could not care less about the sport in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising and dropping the shoulders is a gesture of indifference or not caring.

clue.text: At end of flight, he and I in Paris examine returning A-listers?

indicators.note: at end of means only the last letter of the word flight is taken

parts.note: je is the French word for I

indicators.note: returning means the word for examine is read backwards

parts.note: to test is to examine

explanation.surface: After landing in Paris, a pair of celebrities face a check on the way back.
explanation.definitionFit: The wealthy fashionable people who fly between glamorous places are the celebrities of the social scene.

clue.text: What might be worn by star having drinks?

parts.note: the sun is a star
glasses can be drinks, as in a few glasses of wine

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what a celebrity would wear while out drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' looks like a celebrity, but it is the one in our sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinted spectacles are worn to shield the eyes from bright light.

clue.text: Los Angeles, less than clean

parts.note: under means less than, as in under ten

explanation.surface: A dig at Los Angeles as a city that is not entirely clean.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash clothes, or figuratively to pass dirty money through to make it look legitimate.

clue.text: Diana broadcast about total ban

parts.note: Di is the short form of Diana

indicators.note: about means the word for broadcast goes around the word for total

parts.note: to sow seed by scattering it widely is to broadcast it
all means the total or whole

explanation.surface: Princess Diana speaks on air about a complete prohibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like a radio or TV term but here it is sowing seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse to accept or permit something is to prohibit it.

clue.text: Punishment in Cornish town not unknown

indicators.note: not tells us to remove the unknown from the town's name

parts.note: Penzance is a town in Cornwall, the county at England's south-west tip
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A sentence served in a Cornish town that is not well known.
explanation.definitionFit: An act of self-punishment done to show repentance for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Bliss is being included in pageant

indicators.note: being included in means the word is goes inside the word for pageant

parts.note: a parade is a public procession or pageant

explanation.surface: Pure joy is taking part in a pageant.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven, or any state of perfect happiness, is a synonym of bliss.

clue.text: Club official, person highly prized at close of year

parts.note: a treasure is someone much valued, as in she is a treasure

indicators.note: close of means only the last letter of the word year is used

explanation.surface: A club officer who is cherished at the end of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer who keeps the money and accounts of a club or society.

clue.text: Whisper result, wrongly

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters of the word result are set in a different order

explanation.surface: A rumour of the outcome is spreading, but it is mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft swishing sound, like leaves or silk, akin to a quiet murmur.

clue.text: Only about five crack

indicators.note: about means the word for only goes around the numeral

parts.note: sole means only, as in the sole survivor
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: There are only about five cracks to fix.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a puzzle or code is to work it out.

clue.text: Strong drink for courage

definitions.meaning: a distilled liquor such as whisky or gin
pluck or mettle, as in showing great fight

explanation.surface: Dutch courage: downing a stiff drink to find nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: distilled alcohol, and the vigour or bravery a person shows.

clue.text: Completely at home with everyone

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
all means everyone, as in all are welcome

explanation.surface: Entirely comfortable among everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in total or altogether, as in ten people altogether.

clue.text: Money given to the poor members, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for members is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: arms are limbs, which are members of the body

explanation.surface: Charitable donations made by club members, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent with no sounded R the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable gifts of money or food handed to those in need.

clue.text: Less important matter in fringe publication

parts.note: side means edge or fringe, as in the side of a field
an issue is one edition of a magazine or paper

explanation.surface: A minor topic tucked away in an alternative magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary question that distracts from the main point.

clue.text: Mouth complaint, being briefly sick after thick soup

indicators.note: after means the shortened word for sick follows the soup

parts.note: gumbo is a thick Creole soup or stew from Louisiana

indicators.note: briefly means the word for sick is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: A sore mouth and feeling a bit poorly after eating a thick stew.
explanation.definitionFit: An abscess on the gums, a swelling inside the mouth.

clue.text: Regular payment in post, including gratuity

indicators.note: including means the word for post holds the word for gratuity inside it

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
a tip is a gratuity for service

explanation.surface: A regular salary is in the mail, with a bonus added.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed salary or allowance paid at set intervals, as to a clergyman.
